title: de.hubtask.work.item.updated.v1
description: An item's own fields changed: what was renamed, what was noted. The one item event that is not a snapshot, and deliberately - domain-model.md §4 gives this event a `changeSet` (old and new per field) rather than the object. An update touches one field of an item whose other fields are somebody's notes, so a snapshot on every rename would copy the whole of them into every subscriber's log for a change that did not involve them; what did not change is not announced. Movement and completion have their own events, so a rule that reacts to a rename does not fire when somebody drags a card between lists. Single-value enums stand in for `const`, and the bounds of a value are stated in its description rather than as keywords: the contract test validates against this file with the subset of JSON Schema the project implements, and a keyword it silently ignored would be a promise nobody checks. The wire format is a CloudEvent 1.0 in structured JSON (ADR-0007); the tenant, the actor and the causal chain travel as CloudEvents extension attributes, whose names are lower case without separators as the specification requires. Fields may be added; removing or reinterpreting one requires a .v2 delivered alongside .v1 for at least two minor releases (domain-model.md §4).

id.description: UUIDv7. Stable across delivery attempts, so a consumer deduplicates on it (at-least-once delivery).

source.description: The installation and the bounded context that produced the event.

subject.description: What the event is about, so that a consumer can filter without parsing the payload.

actorid.description: Absent when the system itself acts. No label: an event leaves the installation, and a name is personal data a subscriber does not need in order to react (ADR-0018).

onbehalfof.description: The principal an automation rule or an agent runs as.

correlationid.description: Everything that came out of one original action carries the same value. A root event is its own correlation.

causationid.description: The event that caused this one. Absent for an action a person took.

causationdepth.description: Distance from the original action. The rule engine stops at 5 and marks the run ABORTED_LOOP (automation.md §2).

data.description: What changed, and just enough of the item to place it. No snapshot: the fields that did not change are not here, which is the difference between this event and every other item event.

type.description: The level. Extensible by configuration: a consumer that switches on it must tolerate a value it does not know rather than fail (domain-model.md §1).

collection_id.description: The collection the item belongs to. Sent on every level, because the parent alone does not say which collection an item is in until the whole chain has been walked.

updated_at.description: When the item last changed - the instant of this update.

version.description: The version the change produced. A consumer that also reads the item over REST uses it to tell whether what it fetched is older or newer than this event.

change_set.description: One member per field that moved, keyed by the field name the API uses. Never empty: an update that changes nothing writes nothing and announces nothing. Both sides travel, because a field change trigger fires on "the title became X" as well as on "it stopped being Y", and a payload carrying only the new value can answer the first but never the second. Members may be added as later milestones give the item more fields, so a consumer reads the members it knows and tolerates the ones it does not.

title.description: The item's title, at most 500 code points and on one line.

notes.description: Markdown, unrendered by the server. Only on a type whose profile carries the NOTES capability; the empty string on either side means unset.
